jobs.title: Environmental Scientist / Senior Environmental Scientist – EIA
jobs.description:
Job Description

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Who are we looking for?

We’re looking for an Environmental Scientist / Senior Environmental Scientist – EIA to join WA - Environmental Impact Assessment
team.

Our WA – Environment
business has maintained strong growth in recent years and is currently one of the largest groups in WA, being a leader in impact assessment and approvals, terrestrial ecology, and marine. Our diverse team contributes to a wide variety of projects, with a strategic focus on renewable energy, critical minerals and Defence at a regional, national and global scale.

At GHD, we understand the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance. That’s why we offer flexible working arrangements tailored to support your lifestyle and commitments. This role is open to both full-time
and part-time hours
, with a minimum of 20 hours per week, providing you the flexibility to thrive professionally while balancing your personal life. Join us in an environment that truly values your well-being as much as your expertise.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Conduct comprehensive environmental assessments and impact studies in compliance with Australian regulatory frameworks.
Lead and contribute to the preparation of high-quality proposals and client-ready technical reports following relevant standards and guidelines, client requirements, and GHD project guidelines.
Act as a Project Manager for routine projects, collaborating effectively with project stakeholders to ensure successful client experience in project delivery.
Marketing including the development and submission of proposals for routine, low risk projects which at times may involve convincing internal and external stakeholders.
Communicate with clients about current work and future needs, provide timely updates on project progress.
At senior level, lead project activities and support the development of less experienced team members.

What you will bring to the team:

Bachelor of Science (Environmental) degree or related field.
Sound knowledge of Commonwealth, State and Local Government environmental regulatory requirements.
Applies broad knowledge of a professional discipline or advanced knowledge of technical practices demonstrated in a relevant industry or consulting business.
A track record for delivering exceptional client experience, and an eye for business development opportunities.
Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with diverse stakeholders.
Strong numerical, analytical, and writing skills, including experience in the preparation of reports for clients and or regulators.
Current C class drivers’ licence
Proficient in Microsoft 365 suite (excel, word, outlook)
For candidates at Senior Environmental Scientist level, demonstrated experience in project management, client engagement and supporting the development of less experienced team members.

Interested? Apply now.

Contact Antonia Tomassone

Ph +61 8 6222 8631

GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.

GHD embraces hybrid work arrangements to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive. This supports the diverse needs of our workforce while balancing the benefits of remote working with the value of face-to-face collaboration in the office.

We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.

About Us

Come together and make a meaningful impact.

We bring our people together to create something bigger and solve some of the world's most complex problems. Come and experience the power of commitment and see strategy and ideas come to life when you join GHD.

Let's drive real change.

Our Pledge to You

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

That’s the #PowerOfCommitment

Who We Are

GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents.

The Power of Commitment is our brand promise. It’s what makes us different. We are bound to our stated vision and determination to address humanity’s most urgent needs: to make water, energy and urbanisation sustainable for generations to come.

jobs.title: Principal Toxicologist (Ph.D.)
jobs.description:
About Exponent

Exponent
 is the only premium engineering and scientific consulting firm with the depth and breadth of expertise to solve our clients’ most profoundly unique, unprecedented, and urgent challenges.  

We are committed to engaging multidisciplinary teams of science, engineering, and regulatory experts to empower our clients with solutions that create a safer, healthier, more sustainable world. For over five decades, we've connected the lessons of past failures with tomorrow's solutions to advise clients as they innovate technologically complex products and processes, ensure the safety and health of their users, and address the challenges of sustainability.   

Join our team of experts with degrees from top programs at over 500 universities and extensive experience spanning a variety of industries. At Exponent, you’ll contribute to the diverse pool of ideas, talents, backgrounds, and experiences that drive our collaborative teamwork and breakthrough insights. Plus, we help you grow your career t hrough collaboration, our rich client network, and our excellent support staff . Thanks for your interest in joining our team!

Key statistics: 

950+ Consultants 
640+ Ph.D.s
90+ Disciplines 
30+ Offices globally

Our Opportunity

We are currently seeking a n experienced consultant for a Principal Toxicologist
position in our  Health Sciences  Practice
. This position is open to all U.S. office location s . In this role, you will work as part of a team to provide a high level of leadership and collaboration on projects related to litigation support, toxicological evaluations, risk assessment, and risk communication involving a wide range of products and chemicals . This includes evaluating health hazards, mechanism s of action, dose response, exposure levels , and conducting comparative risk research, utilizing data science tools, assist ing with regulatory documents and analyses , and conducting risk assessments under a variety of regulatory and legal paradigms . As a Principal Toxicologist, you will lead projects, identify new clients, expand relationships with existing clients, develop technical staff, and develop new business in related Health Sciences areas, particularly in the area s of product stewardship, toxic tort, and emerging chemicals of concern. You will be instrumental in helping our clients make and support data-driven and scientifically sound decisions to address today's most pressing issues impacting human health safety.

You will be responsible for

Leverag ing deep knowledge in toxicology to address a wide range of complex human health challenges across diverse client sectors , delivering scientifically rigorous and impactful solutions
Identify ing , pursu ing , and secur ing new client engagements by understanding emerging needs and building long-term partnerships.
Maintain ing and grow ing trusted relationships with existing clients by consistently delivering high-quality work, anticipating future needs, and serving as a strategic advisor.
Build ing , manag ing , and empower ing multidisciplinary teams, fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment that values diverse perspectives and scientific integrity.
Provid ing guidance, coaching, and professional development opportunities to technical staff, supporting their growth into future leaders and experts.
Ensur ing successful project execution through effective planning, resource allocation, and budget management, while maintaining high standards of quality and timeliness.
Offer high-level scientific and strategic advice to both internal stakeholders and external clients, contributing to the firm’s thought leadership and client impact.
Enhance the firm’s visibility and credibility by publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at industry conferences, leading seminars, and participating in expert advisory or technical committees.

You Will Have The Following Skills And Qualifications

PhD in Toxicology or a related scientific field
Minimum of 8 years of consulting experience in the toxicology space
Proven track record of business generation and attracting new and repeat clients or funding
Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology (DABT)
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and make informed recommendations in your scientific field
Outstanding reputation among clients and the scientific community for integrity, responsiveness, and technical expertise
Adept people management abilities coupled with extensive experience in successfully overseeing and executing complex projects
Strong commitment to professional development 

Applicants are encouraged to submit a CV (Curriculum Vitae) with publications (feel free to include publications that are in review or pending) [not restricted to 1 page].

Life @ Exponent

To learn more about life at Exponent and our impact, please visit the following links:

https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

https://www.exponent.com/company/our-impact

 Attracting, inspiring, developing, and rewarding exceptional people with diverse backgrounds and expertise are central to our corporate culture. Our diverse team allows us to provide better value to our clients and enjoy an enriched work environment.

 Our firm is committed to offering a variety of programs and resources to support health and well-being. We believe that providing competitive benefits as well as compensation and recognition programs empowers our staff to do work that makes a difference.

Work Environment

At Exponent, we have found that in-person interactions deepen employee engagement and are crucial for development, for realizing the full potential of our talented and diverse teams, and for building a more inclusive workplace where all have a sense of belonging. In our offices, you can expect a supportive culture and a collaborative, dynamic, multi-disciplinary work environment. Our consultants engage in-person in the office unless they are traveling for client work or other business activities.

We value the rich lives our colleagues enjoy outside of work and understand that work/life balance is critical to our employees and their well-being. Consultants have the autonomy to balance their work and personal schedules so you can meet with clients, visit inspection sites, attend conferences, and make time for priorities outside of work, too. It is this flexible, agile work style and working hours that allow our teams to drive innovation and results in their own ways, while meeting the needs of clients.

Compensation

Our consultants are rewarded for their technical and business contributions and have an opportunity to plan for future success and career growth. Exponent's total compensation plan is consistent with its expectations of the quality and quantity of work performed and with the professional standards set by Exponent. At the Manager level and above, total compensation includes base salary, annual bonus, and 401(k) employer contribution of 7% of base salary.

The base salary range for this position is depending on experience and capabilities which will be assessed during the interview process.

Salary Range

USD $200,000.00 - USD $300,000.00 /Yr.

Benefits You Will Enjoy

Access benefits information on our Life@Exponent page: https://www.exponent.com/careers/life-exponent

Exponent is a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status.

If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability, you may email us at HR-Accommodations@exponent.com .

jobs.title: Consultant, Human Health Risk Assessment and Community Health
jobs.description:
Company Description

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level to mid-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in one of the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

Qualifications

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company! Successful candidates will typically possess:

Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.
Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
GIS capability is a plus.
Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $79,040–$98,800 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

Ready to join us?

If you are passionate about scientific excellence, environmental health, and community impacts, we would love to hear from you.

Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your resume, transcripts, a writing sample and cover letter.

jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Company

Trinity Consultants’ Monitoring Services team is hiring a Senior Air Quality Specialist to install, maintain, and troubleshoot ambient air quality and meteorological monitoring networks for clients across the country. This is a hands-on, field-first role for someone who takes pride in precise, defensible data. You’ll work directly with clients, travel to active monitoring sites, and be trusted to make real-time calls on equipment and data quality.

Schedule & Travel

Hybrid role based between the office and the field; ability to travel 2–5 days a week (transportation provided or compensated). Monday–Friday schedule; occasional weekend work may be required.

Field Operations & Installation

Conduct onsite installation, startup, and commissioning of meteorological and ambient air quality monitoring equipment.
Draw upon hands-on technical experience to perform analyzer maintenance, troubleshooting, and calibrations at remote monitoring sites, minimizing downtime and data loss.
Collect and operate time-integrated samples, and provide proper chain-of-custody documentation to analytical laboratories.
Apply practical field experience to support the design, integration, and build-out of ambient air quality monitoring systems.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

Maintain current audit and calibration certifications, and apply working knowledge of EPA and state monitoring protocols in the field.
Provide QA of air quality audit and calibration reports.
Review incoming data with an experienced eye to proactively flag instrumentation issues before they affect data quality.
Provide proper documentation and record keeping for all air quality systems and network servicing and auditing.

Client & Program Support

Provide meteorological sensor and air quality instrument calibration, maintenance, and audit services for numerous clients across the U.S., with a concentration in California.

Qualifications

4–8+ years of hands-on field experience in ambient air quality or meteorological monitoring; a Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, meteorology, or engineering may be considered in place of equivalent field experience.

Required Skills

Demonstrated, practical experience with DC electronics, telemetry, and remote data logging equipment.
Working knowledge of state and Federal (EPA) environmental monitoring guidelines and regulations, gained through direct application at active monitoring sites.
Hands-on mechanical and electrical troubleshooting experience.
Strong work ethic, attention to detail, and proven problem-solving skills; comfortable working independently and as part of a team.

Preferred Skills

Proven, hands-on experience operating and maintaining meteorological and air quality instrumentation.
Experience-based client interaction and communication skills, including strong active listening developed through direct client-facing field work.
Proficiency in the MS365 ecosystem (Teams, SharePoint, OneNote, etc.).

Pay range and compensation package

Our Santa Clarita office offers the stability of a corporate company with the atmosphere and camaraderie of a small, family-run business. We’re intentional about cultivating a fun, healthy environment for our team.

Competitive pay
401(k)
Dental insurance
Health insurance
Life insurance
Paid time off
Paid travel time, expenses, and daily per diem

Equal Opportunity Statement

This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of duties. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to lift 70 lbs, travel freely and frequently, and remain on feet for up to 12 hours per day at field sites; multi-day field efforts are not uncommon. While performing site work, employees may occasionally be exposed to moving mechanical parts, high or precarious places, fumes or airborne particles, and toxic or caustic chemicals. Noise levels at monitoring sites are typically moderate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken. Comfort with basic math and algebra as applied to air quality measurements (percentages, area, volume, and similar calculations). Sound judgment interpreting instructions and troubleshooting variable field conditions where standardization is limited.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level to mid-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in one of the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

Qualifications

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company! Successful candidates will typically possess:

Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.
Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
GIS capability is a plus.
Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $79,040–$98,800 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ready to join us?

new_jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Specialist
new_jobs.description:
About the Company

Trinity Consultants’ Monitoring Services team is hiring a Senior Air Quality Specialist to install, maintain, and troubleshoot ambient air quality and meteorological monitoring networks for clients across the country. This is a hands-on, field-first role for someone who takes pride in precise, defensible data. You’ll work directly with clients, travel to active monitoring sites, and be trusted to make real-time calls on equipment and data quality.

Schedule & Travel

Hybrid role based between the office and the field; ability to travel 2–5 days a week (transportation provided or compensated). Monday–Friday schedule; occasional weekend work may be required.

Field Operations & Installation

Conduct onsite installation, startup, and commissioning of meteorological and ambient air quality monitoring equipment.
Draw upon hands-on technical experience to perform analyzer maintenance, troubleshooting, and calibrations at remote monitoring sites, minimizing downtime and data loss.
Collect and operate time-integrated samples, and provide proper chain-of-custody documentation to analytical laboratories.
Apply practical field experience to support the design, integration, and build-out of ambient air quality monitoring systems.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

Maintain current audit and calibration certifications, and apply working knowledge of EPA and state monitoring protocols in the field.
Provide QA of air quality audit and calibration reports.
Review incoming data with an experienced eye to proactively flag instrumentation issues before they affect data quality.
Provide proper documentation and record keeping for all air quality systems and network servicing and auditing.

Client & Program Support

Provide meteorological sensor and air quality instrument calibration, maintenance, and audit services for numerous clients across the U.S., with a concentration in California.

Qualifications

4–8+ years of hands-on field experience in ambient air quality or meteorological monitoring; a Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, meteorology, or engineering may be considered in place of equivalent field experience.

Required Skills

Demonstrated, practical experience with DC electronics, telemetry, and remote data logging equipment.
Working knowledge of state and Federal (EPA) environmental monitoring guidelines and regulations, gained through direct application at active monitoring sites.
Hands-on mechanical and electrical troubleshooting experience.
Strong work ethic, attention to detail, and proven problem-solving skills; comfortable working independently and as part of a team.

Preferred Skills

Proven, hands-on experience operating and maintaining meteorological and air quality instrumentation.
Experience-based client interaction and communication skills, including strong active listening developed through direct client-facing field work.
Proficiency in the MS365 ecosystem (Teams, SharePoint, OneNote, etc.).

Pay range and compensation package

Our Santa Clarita office offers the stability of a corporate company with the atmosphere and camaraderie of a small, family-run business. We’re intentional about cultivating a fun, healthy environment for our team.

Competitive pay
401(k)
Dental insurance
Health insurance
Life insurance
Paid time off
Paid travel time, expenses, and daily per diem

Equal Opportunity Statement

This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not an exhaustive list of duties. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to lift 70 lbs, travel freely and frequently, and remain on feet for up to 12 hours per day at field sites; multi-day field efforts are not uncommon. While performing site work, employees may occasionally be exposed to moving mechanical parts, high or precarious places, fumes or airborne particles, and toxic or caustic chemicals. Noise levels at monitoring sites are typically moderate.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Ability to communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken. Comfort with basic math and algebra as applied to air quality measurements (percentages, area, volume, and similar calculations). Sound judgment interpreting instructions and troubleshooting variable field conditions where standardization is limited.
